sights.w: Small shrine at the edge of Tennōji Park, said to have been founded by Prince Shōtoku for his uncle Emperor Sushun while Shitennō-ji was being built; one of Shitennō-ji's seven associated shrines and known as the shrine that grants 'one wish in a lifetime'. Named for the moat once crossed to reach it.

Hilltop shrine to Emperor Nintoku, founded by imperial decree in 866 at the reputed site of the Naniwa Takatsu Palace and moved here when Hideyoshi built Osaka Castle; famous as the setting of classic rakugo stories, with rakugo still performed in the grounds. Rebuilt after WWII air raids (one Edo-period storehouse survived).

sights.n: Kōnoike Shinden Kaisho (鴻池新田会所)
sights.address: Kōnoike Motomachi, Higashi-Ōsaka, Osaka (5 min walk from JR Kōnoike-Shinden Station)
sights.w: Estate office built in 1707 by the Kōnoike merchant house to run the farmland reclaimed after the Yamato River was rerouted; the main house and four storehouses were designated Important Cultural Properties in 1980, and the grounds keep a stroll garden. Rare surviving Edo-period land-development office.

sights.n: Tsurumi Ryokuchi (Expo '90 Commemorative Park, 花博記念公園鶴見緑地)
sights.w: 122-hectare park on the site of the 1990 International Garden and Greenery Exposition, home to the giant Sakuya Konohana Kan greenhouse, seasonal flower gardens, BBQ, camping and sports grounds; free entry except some facilities.
